column3: For every terminal set and specified full minimum tree, a degeneration must attain the different minimum-Steiner-point objective. Topology-preserving edge contraction need not optimize that objective; no uniform contraction mechanism established.

Universal automorphisms of every finitely generated exponential-growth group require orbit-product growth, not just ball growth for the identity. Inner automorphisms are only the weaker subquestion; no full-scope reduction established.

All simple drawings and all k with the quadratic edge threshold are required. Sparse disconnected drawings suggest testing but the oriented k-edge convention for incomplete graphs must first be recovered. No geometric witness or primary definition clearance.

Literal statement already reports n=11563 as a published obstruction to the all-n determinant divisibility claim. No determinant computation or original proof body replay here; do not recredit that witness.

Every k and every finite-abelian graded PI algebra require a comparison of relatively free graded growth with the identity component. The PI-exponent analogy supplies no GK-dimension bridge; even notation Z2 versus G needs primary checking.

Product is invariant under taking complements, so a star equality also gives equality for its complement. Correcting the asymmetric iff clause is wording-only and earns no credit; the universal eigenvalue bound still needs actual primary/prior bodies.
Monotonicity concerns the extremum over all Latin squares at every successive order. Arbitrary padding can destroy Latin constraints; embeddings into larger orders do not prove the n-to-n+1 step.

Exactly half the maximum even-factor degree is required at the Dirac threshold. Approximate packing and high-minimum-degree theorems do not give exact packing there. No short route across extremal configurations.

Countability at the identity trace bound cannot be inferred from continuum-many reals at n^(1+epsilon). A uniform coding/countability argument for all functionals is absent; finite trace checks cannot resolve it.

For every strongly positive basis and every lattice point, existence and uniqueness of pointed elements must both hold. The two named bases are parameter instances; positivity alone has not supplied a general change-of-basis argument.

Exact extension distinguishing number nine needs both all-prescribed-coloring extension and a sharp obstruction under the precise sphere action. The cube lower bound alone is insufficient and the action convention needs primary recovery.

Primary arXiv1407.1276v1 Conjecture1.1 and Theorem2.1 explicitly replace 2n-4 by sharp n-1 at odd order. Read local theorem/proof; underlying graphical-sequence lemmas not fully audited. Exact n5 graph check is only an instance of that known refutation.

The connected all-graph bound couples total absolute spectral mass with sqrt(lambda1). Standard energy Cauchy-Schwarz gives a different n-dependent estimate; no uniform bridge or exact violating graph established.

All tau in the genus-two fundamental domain and three specified transformations require control of Borchardt square-root branches. Numerical mean iteration cannot prove the global branch identity; notation references are incomplete in the record.

An edge inactive in every tree is a common-intersection assertion for an arbitrary strongly Tutte-descriptive activity. A decision-tree activity would supply a last-tested edge but the equivalence to all such activities is precisely the unresolved bridge. Primary v3 HTML 404; no alternative fishing.

The explicit leading constant for each fixed integer moment n>=2 requires sharp ideal-count convolution, including the borderline second moment. Order-of-growth estimates and finite numerical constants do not establish the displayed asymptotic.

Every minor-critical tree-depth-k graph must have maximum degree at most k-1. Criticality does not directly force a low-degree elimination root; checking small obstruction catalogues would not establish all k.

A full disproof needs a positive n not divisible by three and a finite covering certificate blocking every repeated digit at every appended length. Trial primality at finitely many lengths cannot prove c(n)=0; no covering route established.

Non-D-finiteness requires a global analytic or differential-algebraic obstruction for the reciprocal avoidance series. Finite coefficient guessing or failure to find an ODE is insufficient; no such obstruction established.

The statement itself reports a counterexample in its source. No knot-exterior/surgery proof body replay here; this is a prior lead with no discovery eligibility, not an independently verified refutation.

The identity ranges over all s>=r-1 and polynomial indices; the source definitions of S,T and admissible r are missing from the record. Cancellation may be a telescoping route but no complete recurrence bridge or parameter domain has been recovered.

The all-m coefficient formula is short but Lambda_m and its coefficient convention are not defined in this literal record. Inclusion-exclusion of three-state terms would only be a heuristic until tied to the exact maximum-likelihood degree object.

All integer search depths h<=n/k and all k>=2 need matching strategies in a continuous hiding game. Counting discrete multiset placements might give one bound, but arbitrary real depths and adaptive search prevent inferring the exact value.

Removing a corner must preserve extremality for every nonempty extremal class, not merely maximum classes. Compression does not preserve the needed deletion certificate. No bounded full-scope route; successor literature not cleared.

Every nontrivial two-variable word must hit every PSL2(C) conjugacy class, especially nonsemisimple unipotents. Dominance or generic trace surjectivity does not cover exceptional fibers; no uniform word mechanism.

The Delta+2 acyclic edge-color bound is uniform in all graphs. Product-graph bounds and ordinary edge coloring do not prevent bichromatic cycles in arbitrary graphs; no short constructive recoloring proof.

Equivalence of unimodality for every positive convolution power under the classical-free correspondence requires both implications on all infinitely divisible laws. Checking smooth or atomic examples does not resolve the Levy-measure characterization.

Every closed pre-foam must have choice-independent evaluation through several local reductions. Critical-pair confluence is plausible only after all tetrahedral/monodromy rules are specified; a full chain is outside bounded screening.

Uniform constant-factor optimality of q(n) for union-free families requires the actual q construction and union-free convention. A rough exponential upper bound does not compare to the specific lower bound.

The name harmonic index and symbol R' do not determine the reciprocal degree weight. Complete proper colorings suggest charging color-pair edges, but no charging inequality is claimed without reading the exact index definition.

All symmetrizable Cartan matrices and symmetrizers require the full root/rank-vector correspondence. The Dynkin and symmetric cases do not extend by a finite parameter calculation; no small full-scope mechanism.

Large finite negative curvature, symmetric group, inertia and demand require exact definitions and quantitative hypotheses. A symmetry-fixed vertex alone does not force both extremal properties; no wording-based counterexample receives credit.

For every alpha satisfying condition L the mass interval is asserted forbidden for small-data global solvability. The nonlinearity sign and solution/data spaces are essential; a linear or special-alpha example would not resolve the source scope.

The all-k hamiltonicity claim already reports a 3-diregular circulant on 12 vertices as a source counterexample. No independent Hamilton-cycle exclusion computation or primary proof replay here; no new credit.

The exact Gaussian identity involves a limiting auxiliary function in dimensions 8 and24 for all potential parameters. Exceptional-lattice optimality alone does not identify this limit or justify the Fourier limit interchange.

Uniform unprovability is quantified over theories and monotone computable families, with H dominating all T-provably-total functions. Pointwise domination does not automatically produce a proof-in-T reduction; no diagonal construction meeting every assumption established.

The all-knot height identity uses the maximum thick-sphere count over thin positions. Concatenating positions provides no optimality for all thin positions of the sum; satellite phenomena and later bodies need checking.

The trunk identity needs both upper and lower bounds for every pair of knots. Stacking gives a plausible upper construction; the lower bound needs a genuine topological theorem, with likely successor literature. No original route established.

Every knot exterior must have rank equal to Heegaard genus t+1. The easy rank upper bound is not the lower bound; constructing generators or checking particular knot families gives no full-scope outcome.

All rational linear relations of multiple zeta values at unrestricted weights must follow from the integral-series relations. Weight17 dimension computations are only evidence; missing identity notation also needs primary recovery.

Every simple n-regular balanced 3-partite hypergraph must have an n-1 matching. Latin-square transversals form a narrower case; general hypergraph examples require exact simplicity/regularity verification. No bounded obstruction found or sweep run.

Exact maxima of two different spectral functionals for every n require sharp universal inequalities and matching extremizers. Numerical named-graph testing cannot certify either maximum; no bridge from spectral radius to all positive eigenvalues established.
